subject: Private deployment IaC: merge policy, module ownership & soft-fail pattern
messages:
From: Alan Kim <alan.kim@infra-consult.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>; acme-devops@acme.com
Cc: terraform-mods@vendor.io
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Merge policy for private IaC modules + CI soft-fail proposal

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call with Acme SRE, I'm attaching an updated IaC bundle (priv-iactemplate-v2.zip) that contains the proposed Terraform modules, Helm charts, and ansible roles for their single-tenant VPC deployment. Two quick asks:

1) Merge policy: Acme needs clarity on when a module change is allowed straight to master vs. must go through canary/staging deploy gates. They want to avoid late surprises in on-prem smoke runs.
2) CI soft-fail: their on-prem test runners intermittently time out when talking to on-prem hardware. We propose a "soft-fail" stage in CI that doesn't block PR merges for non-prod branches but creates an automatic ticket and tags the PR for manual gating. Need your guidance on how this interacts with Redwood's security/compliance constraints (prod must be hard-gated).

I've pasted a short summary of failing jobs we saw in the last run in the attachment ci-failure-log.txt.

Can your team review the bundle and advise owner assignment for network/helm/ansible modules and whether the soft-fail pattern is acceptable?

Thanks,
Alan
Infra-Consult
Attachment: priv-iactemplate-v2.zip (application/zip)
Attachment: ci-failure-log.txt (text/plain)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alan Kim <alan.kim@infra-consult.com>
Cc: acme-devops@acme.com, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Merge policy for private IaC modules + CI soft-fail proposal

Alan — thanks for the bundle and logs. Looping in Irene (network lead) and Marcus (CI/runtime) to get concrete recommendations.

Initial thoughts:
- We should enforce hard gates for any TF that touches routing/firewalls or KMS key material. Those changes must go through staging canaries and an on-call approve step.
- Non-prod modules (observability, minor helm defaults) can follow the proposed soft-fail pattern as long as the PR includes an automated remediation/issue generation flow and a defined SLA for triage (48h).

Next steps: can we sync on Monday for a 30-min alignment? Also, Alan: please share the GitHub PR link (if available) — easier to comment inline than on the zip.

Thanks,
Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Alan Kim <alan.kim@infra-consult.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Merge policy for private IaC modules + CI soft-fail proposal

Thanks for looping me in. I pulled the network TF and the helm overlays from the bundle. A few concrete items: 

- Module ownership: we need an explicit OWNERS file at the module root listing at least one Redwood owner + one Acme owner. Without that the module should be marked "unowned" and require a security review before merging.
- Network defaults: make default state explicit (deny-by-default for ingress and egress) and include a named security policy set. That reduces accidental wide-open egress in on-prem installs.
- Helm charts: add a small non-prod values file (values.staging.yaml) and a schema for allowed overrides so that Acme's CD system can't inject unsafe settings.

I've attached an updated network diagram with annotations (network-diagram-vpc-2026.png) to show the recommended AZ-level NAT egress and management-plane isolation.

On the soft-fail idea: acceptable for staging/testing if the CI produces an automated ticket (we use JIRA) with the failure artifact and an owner assigned. For prod branches (main/prod) the CI must hard-block and require a manual security sign-off. This maps to our SOC2 control expectations for change management and segregation.

Attachment: network-diagram-vpc-2026.png (image/png)

Irene
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alan Kim <alan.kim@infra-consult.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Merge policy for private IaC modules + CI soft-fail proposal

Quick update from the CI side after running the zip through the on-prem runners: 
- Failure pattern: intermittent ansible connection timeouts to the management NIC during hardware snapshotting (see ci-failure-log.txt). These failures are network flakiness, not config drift.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/452 contains the split modules (terraform/network, terraform/compute, helm/monitoring, ansible/provision).

Proposed CI changes: 
1) Introduce a new pipeline phase "validation-soft" that runs on PRs for non-prod branches. If validation-soft fails, mark the PR with label "validation:soft-fail", auto-create a JIRA with reproduction artifacts, and proceed to run lint and internal unit tests.
2) For prod/main branch PRs, put the old behavior back: "validation-hard" must succeed. No merges allowed until successful.
3) Add a lightweight owners check plugin at merge time: if OWNERS file missing, block the merge and tag with "owners:missing".

I've created a failing Jenkins job URL (jenkins/priv-deploy-job/branches/PR-452) with the exact run for reference. The soft-fail stage will require a short-term exception in policy (we will document it).

Marcus
Engineering Manager, Infra Runtime
Attachment: ci-failure-log.txt (text/plain)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Kim <alan.kim@infra-consult.com>, acme-devops@acme.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Merge policy for private IaC modules + CI soft-fail proposal

Thanks team — this is reasonable. Two management clarifications: 

- Prod gating: absolutely no soft-fail for main/prod. Any change that could affect routing, secrets, KMS must have a human approver and a staged canary.
- Timeline: we should treat the owners and OWNERS-file requirement as blocking for the next release window. Can we aim to have OWNERS files in the repo and the validation-soft stage implemented by EOD Friday (2026-03-27)? If not, escalate and provide a plan.

Also, please itemize the acceptance criteria for the soft-fail flow (what fields in the JIRA, how long until triage, who gets auto-notified).

-Lauren
Director, Product Operations
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Kim <alan.kim@infra-consult.com>, acme-devops@acme.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Merge policy for private IaC modules + CI soft-fail proposal

Summary / next steps (agreed):
- OWNERS files: repository owners required for each module. Owners file template to be added to /docs/OWNERS-template.md (owner: Irene). Due: 2026-03-27.
- CI validation-soft: implement new pipeline phase that tags PRs on non-prod soft failures, creates a JIRA with artifacts, and does not block merges. Owner: Marcus. Target: 2026-03-27.
- Hard-gates for prod: any TF touching networking/KMS/secrets must require validation-hard pass + manual sign-off.
- Acceptance criteria for soft-fail JIRA: failure artifact attached, failure type (ansible/conn-timeout/log-id), assigned owner = module OWNERS, triage SLA = 48h.
- Documentation: update private-deploy/runbooks/priv-iac-checklist (owner: Tessa).

I'll file the internal tracking ticket and create the PR comments for https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/452 with the above items. Thanks everyone — looping Acme to confirm they are ok with owners + soft-fail for staging.

Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
